questions.q: In the order a decoder-style transformer block actually runs, what comes immediately after the first LayerNorm?
options: The feed-forward sublayer
A residual add straight to the output
Causal self-attention
A second LayerNorm
questions.explain: The block is LayerNorm, then causal self-attention, then a residual add, then LayerNorm again, then feed-forward, then a residual add.

questions.q: In `x = x + attn(norm1(x))`, what makes this call self-attention rather than cross-attention?
options: The `attn_mask` argument is set to `None`
The same normalized tensor is passed as query, key, and value
`nn.MultiheadAttention` is only capable of self-attention
The residual add happens after the call
questions.explain: Self-attention means Q, K, and V all come from the same source tensor. Here `h = norm1(x)` is passed as all three arguments to `self.attn(h, h, h, ...)`.

questions.q: A `TransformerBlock` receives input of shape (B, T, d_model). What shape does it return?
options: (B, T, d_model) — unchanged
(B, T, d_ff)
(B, T * num_heads, d_model)
(B, d_model) — pooled over the sequence
questions.explain: Neither sublayer nor the residual adds change the shape. Output is always (B, T, d_model), which is exactly what lets you stack blocks.

questions.q: Why does the block's `forward` method accept an `attn_mask` parameter instead of building the causal mask itself?
options: PyTorch requires every module to take a mask argument
The mask depends on the full sequence length and is built once by the model that owns the block, then passed to every block
Attention masks are only used during evaluation, never training
It's a bug — the mask should be built inside the block
questions.explain: The mask depends on T and is the same for every block in the stack, so it's built once (in Lesson 40's TinyGPT) and passed into each block's forward call.

questions.q: Why is `need_weights=False` passed to `self.attn(...)` in the block's forward pass?
options: It disables attention entirely for faster debugging
It's required for causal masking to work
It skips computing and returning the full attention-weight matrix, which isn't needed for training or inference
It reduces the number of attention heads used
questions.explain: `nn.MultiheadAttention` can return attention weights for inspection, but computing and returning them has a cost. Setting `need_weights=False` skips that when you only need the output.
